c.h:
This guide outlines the most effective methods to train Invention, RuneScape's only elite skill. While Invention is a skill that incorporates many different mechanics, the primary training method is to augment equipment, level the equipment level by using the augmented item(s), and then disassemble or siphon the items for experience. As players level up in the skill, they can also discover blueprints, awarding them large but non-repeatable experience gains. Levelling Invention typically happens by actively participating in another skill. This contrasts with how almost all other skills are trained, where levelling the skill is done by actively training that skill only.

Due to Invention's status as an elite skill, gaining Invention experience has slightly different mechanics than gaining experience in a non-elite skill.

In order to unlock the Invention skill, players must first have at least level 80 in Crafting, Divination, and Smithing. Players who meet these requirements should head to the Invention Guild, located northeast of the Falador lodestone. Players must talk to Doc to complete the Invention Tutorial before levelling Invention through other means.

As RuneScape's only elite skill, Invention is subject to a number of unique mechanics and quirks not found with other skills. First, the experience curve for Invention is different from that of other skills. Early levels in Invention require more experience compared to standard skills, but later levels require less experience. Overall, to train the skill to level 120, about 23 million less total experience is required. Due to Invention's status as an elite skill, lamps and stars redeemed on Invention give half the XP amount they usually would, leaving this as a less efficient choice in the long run compared to XP boosting another skill the player has trouble with. This also includes Tears of Guthix.

Disassembly and siphoning are unique in that they are not affected by any experience boosts (e.g. torstol incense sticks or Double XP Live). However, other sources of Invention experience, such as discovery, are affected by boosts. Invention interacts uniquely with Double XP Live: augmented items gain item experience at 1.5x the usual rate, and other experience sources yield 1.5x the usual experience.

A charged XP Capacitor 5000 is an item purchasable from the Grand Exchange. When you have an activated XP Capacitor 5000 in your inventory, gaining item experience will also "drain" the same amount of experience from the XP Capacitor, essentially doubling the item experience gain. XP Capacitors start with 100,000 item experience, and once this is all drained, the item crumbles to dust. The XP Capacitor effectively doubles experience rates, and every player training Invention should consider using them. The price to purchase a single XP Capacitor from the Grand Exchange is 1,745,257 gp. This item does not work with protean cogs.

The Enlightened perk increases the rate at which the item gains experience. Since your Invention experience rate is based on how quickly you can siphon or disassemble items at a particular level, this perk directly increases your experience rate. Each level of Enlightened, up to 4, increases your experience rates by 3%. The below table lists recommended gizmo layouts for low- and high-level players to create the Enlightened perk.

At level 77, players can discover the blueprint for the mechanised siphon. The mechanised siphon can be configured to automatically siphon items once they hit a certain equipment level. This ensures that your items are siphoned as soon as possible, and it minimises "wasted" item experience that may be lost when manually siphoning items that are over the threshold for levelling up.

The Scavenging perk grants a percent chance to receive uncommon Invention materials upon killing an enemy. Using this perk will not increase experience rates, but it can potentially yield hundreds of millions of GP in terms of Invention materials when training the skill through combat. In particular, Scavenging 4 is recommended for an armour gizmo, because it gives a chance to obtain rare Invention materials, many of which are extremely expensive or difficult to obtain otherwise (e.g. noxious components or third-age components). As a result, using Scavenging 4 throughout Invention training can yield hundreds of millions' worth of components. Scavenging 4 can be created starting at level 85, when Ancient Invention is unlocked.

For most players, the primary method of levelling Invention will be through combat, which in particular involves killing large hordes of monsters. As a result, equipment and abilities that allow you to deal area-of-effect damage are highly recommended. Here is a non-exhaustive list of certain equipment:

Corruption Shot/Corruption Blast

For players who plan on training through Ranged or Magic combat, the Corruption Shot or Corruption Blast ability is recommended. Both abilities have the same effect, and differ only in the combat style. The abilities apply a powerful bleed that spreads to nearby enemies. One ability can be unlocked by reading a Mazcab ability codex (32,964,929 gp).

Mechanised Chinchompa

The mechanised chinchompa is a tier 75 ranged weapon that makes ranged abilities also strike enemies within 1 square of your primary target (3x3 area in total). This weapon easily doubles or triples your damage when using ranged. Even though it is not augmentable, it can be used with an augmented off-hand to yield experience rates much higher than using "normal" ranged weaponry.

Greater Chain

The Greater Chain Magic ability hits multiple targets and has the effect of "duplicating" your next magic ability cast onto the secondary targets for half damage. It can be obtained by reading its codex (210,056,320 gp).

Halberd

For players who prefer Melee combat, a halberd is recommended, because it allows powerful melee abilities such as Hurricane, Meteor Strike or a dragon 2h sword stored in an Essence of Finality amulet to have greater reach.

Optimal halberd weapons include Laniakea's spear, dragon rider lance, noxious scythe and Tumeken's Light. Use the best weapon possible, unless aiming for a specific perk such as Aftershock or Biting.

The basic ways to train Invention to level 120 are shown in the following table. Experience gains when using a capacitor are doubled, except for creating gizmos. In general, training invention through combat is much faster than training through skilling. It is recommended that you follow your respective combat training guide for recommended methods. Due to the high variability of players' XPM during combat training, it is difficult to estimate a player's XPM rate while doing combat. However, since you are free to do combat however you like, you can easily train Invention while performing other activities, such as Slayer or bossing.

  • Skilling is the slowest way to train Invention, but it can be done while training other skills.
  • The method recommended to most players is to go through combat and use equipment siphons when items reach either level 9 (for an overall faster XP gain) or level 12 (for lower costs).
  • The most expensive and fastest but no combat required - manufacture ancient weapon or armour gizmos from scratch where all slots are filled with timeworn components.

While training Invention, players unlock the ability to discover blueprints, which award large one-time experience drops. This experience should not be ignored; see the discovery section for more details.

Completing the Invention tutorial with Perfect optimisation on discoveries will put you at level 4. In the event that you did not get enough experience from discoveries in the tutorial, you can quickly disassemble items to make up for any remaining experience (for instance, disassembling a yew longbow gives 12 experience).

Once you reach level 4, you should immediately research the maximum equipment level 5 blueprint. After this, 186,000 experience is needed for level 27. The fastest way to gain this experience is by using an augmentor to augment two tier 70-75 combat equipment, training the augmented equipment to level 5, and then disassembling them. Invention experience is granted once the item is disassembled; the item and the augmentor will be lost. A highly cost-efficient method is to disassemble two augmented black salamanders at level 5. The cost is 4,270 gp for the salamanders, 730,606 gp for the augmentors; 4270+730606 gp in total. You would need harralander tar as ammo to use with augmented black salamanders like its unaugmented counterpart.

To level augmented combat items, you must use them in combat. The higher the combat experience gained, the higher the Invention experience, so you should partake in combat that grants high experience rates.

Divine charge crafting

A cost-effective but slow method for training Invention is to mass-disassemble common items for simple parts and then craft divine charges with them. Items such as magic logs have extremely low junk chances and will disassemble almost 1:1 into simple parts while providing 2 Invention experience per item. Crafting divine charges with 20 simple parts and a number of divine energy (such as 225 Incandescent energy) will yield 220 Invention experience and 80 Divination experience, and the resulting charge can sell on the Grand Exchange for a small profit.

To get from level 5 to 22 using this method will require approximately 6,972 magic logs and 74,700 incandescent energy or equivalent, and will take around 2-3 hours.

c.h:
At level 27, you should immediately use Discovery for two very important blueprints. First, you can discover the ability to train augmented equipment to level 10. Second, you also unlock the equipment siphon, which can be used on an item to drain its item experience for Invention experience without destroying the item or its augmentor.

Once siphoning has been unlocked, it becomes the recommended method for levelling Invention. Disassembling common items is far too slow and is no longer an effective way to gain experience. Additionally, augmented black salamanders and other cheap augmentable gear are slow to level compared to high-level equipment (such as mechanised chinchompas paired with an augmented off-hand and augmented armour). If you do choose to disassemble anyway, it should be done when the item is level 10, because this both maximises the experience rate and minimises the GP loss from losing the item and its augmentor.

Higher-tier augmented equipment yields more experience than lower-tier equipment. When siphoning to train Invention, higher-tier equipment should be preferred if possible. Siphoning equipment should be done when the item is either level 9 or 12. Level 9 yields higher experience, while level 12 is cheaper.

At this point, you should consider using XP Capacitor 5000, which double item experience rate and thus effectively double Invention experience rates. If using XP Capacitors, siphon at level 9; it is no longer cost-effective to siphon at level 12.

There are two main ways to level up Invention: Combat and Skilling. Levelling items is recommended for most players to train the skill up to level 120.

c.h:
Combat is the fastest repeatable method to level Invention. Players should equip a full set of augmented gear when training combat. This includes an augmented main hand weapon, augmented off-hand weapon if applicable, augmented body, and augmented legs. The ability to augment leg armour must be researched using an Invention blueprint available at level 45 (level 40 when drinking an extreme invention potion). In addition, the highest tier gear should be preferred, as it yields higher experience rates.

Equipment experience for combat items is a function of combat experience, so you generally want to choose combat encounters that give fast combat experience rates, which typically only happens when fighting against groups of enemies. Equipment experience for items is gained per hit, so other forms of damage (e.g. familiars) does not grant equipment experience. The combat efficiency boosts lists certain unlocks and equipment that can greatly increase your area-of-effect damage and experience rates. If you do not have Greater Chain, melee or ranged combat will typically yield the highest experience rates.

You may choose to level Invention by participating in any combat activity of your choice, e.g. Slayer tasks. However, if you are solely focused on the fastest experience rates possible, the below two methods are recommended.

Shattered Worlds

An alternative way of levelling up Invention very rapidly is via combat in Shattered Worlds, although it has high gear requirements. Deaths in Shattered Worlds are safe, though signs of life and equivalent will not activate even if not on cooldown.

This requires the player to use a world bracket that has the Feeling pumped mutator offered, which grants full adrenaline for ten seconds when activated.

When using ranged, bring Mechanised chinchompas to deal AoE damage and an off-hand crossbow to maximise damage. Try to clump melee monsters towards rangers or magers so they can get the most benefit from the damage. The player also needs to use an Essence of Finality amulet with a dark bow in order to use its special attack, which is very likely to kill enemies off in a single strike.

When using melee, bring a halberd-type weapon; ideally a noxious scythe or Tumeken's Light, along with an essence of finality amulet with a dragon 2h sword in it. Two special attacks will kill off enemies.

Additionally, XP Capacitor 5000s are recommended to increase experience gain. Clear warded chests and pick the hydra debuff when possible, as these give more enemies to kill.

The best worlds to train through this method are the world brackets 91-95 or 116-120, as enemies here have enough health and don't deal as much damage compared to other brackets. 116-120 is most optimal, but players who are struggling to survive may want to use 91-95 instead.

As many enemies are slain through this method, melee users should have Scavenging on their weapon to obtain additional components while levelling their equipment.

An alternative to combat is to train tools to gain Invention experience. In general, due to the high cost of buying augmentable tools, they should only be siphoned and not disassembled. Tools offer a less intensive method to train Invention at an overall lower Invention experience rate (mostly because only one item is trained at a time). An exception to this is using an augmented crystal fishing rod at the Fishing Frenzy activity at the Deep Sea Fishing Hub. At level 99 Fishing, at least 26,300 item experience per hour can be obtained via this method. This can be increased through the use of the fishing outfit or shark outfit, as well as adding the perks Enlightened and Wise with gizmos. One can reach item level 9 in just over 1 hour of play; and level 12 in just over 3 hours of play. Once the initial time investment in discovering how to make them is done, the cost of creating new crystal fishing rods is negligible, rendering them a less costly item to disassemble than the much more expensive top tier combat weapons and gear or other crystal tools like the hatchet and pickaxe. Tools also drain charge at a much lower rate, reducing cost.

Augmenting tools requires research at level 22: augmented hatchets, pickaxes, mattocks and/or the fishing rod-o-matic. Tools benefit from having higher Woodcutting/Fishing levels to access higher experience rate methods, as the equipment experience rate is directly tied to the base skilling experience rate for that tool. The fishing rod-o-matic functions as an augmented item but does not require an augmentor. Cheaper items such as the Fishing rod-o-matic or Pyro-matic may be disassembled for higher experience, but more expensive items such as dragon or most crystal items are generally siphoned and not disassembled.

In the event that there are multiple identical augmented tools in one's bank - such as augmented crystal hammers - and a bank preset utilising the equipment tab is used, the preset will cycle through each of the augmented tools; each time prioritising the one with the lowest item experience. As such, it is advised to keep only one version of an augmented tool at a time or to not use the equipment tab when creating a bank preset.

While training Invention, putting perks on your gear can increase your combat efficiency and thus your XPM. Since you retain gizmos upon disassembly or siphoning, using a low-level perk setup is highly recommended, since these perks can last for many levels throughout your training.

While using black salamanders is technically the highest XP ratio, actually levelling the salamanders will likely be very difficult due to their lacklustre damage and lack of access to mechanised chinchompas, so disassembling them is not recommended.

While training Invention, players will unlock new blueprints to discover on the Invention workbench. Once experience is gained from discovering a blueprint, the blueprint cannot be discovered again. While discovery is not the main source of experience, discovering all blueprints ranging from levels 1 to 118 yields over 10.8 million experience. Therefore, discovering blueprints should not be neglected. In addition to discovering blueprints at their own level, players can consume super or extreme invention potions to boost their Invention level, allowing them to discover blueprints up to 17 levels above their actual level.

When discovering items, it is very important to get a Perfect optimisation on your blueprints in order to get the maximum amount of experience.

A knowledge bomb or Double XP Live will increase discovery experience by 25% or 50% respectively; therefore, one can consider waiting to discover non-essential blueprints until those boosts are available.

Creating gizmos yields the fastest Invention experience by far, but it is also extremely expensive. As such, it can only be recommended to players who seek the absolute fastest training method and do not care about cost. You can craft weapon, armour, or tool gizmo shells and then fill them with materials that yield a high amount of experience. Both crafting the shell and creating the gizmo will grant experience. Gizmo experience is equal to the sum of the experience granted by each individual material (see materials article). It is important to note that you must unlock ancient gizmos by either crafting the 'Ancient gizmos' blueprint or by buying it form the GE and researching it on the invention table.

At level 86, players can drink an extreme invention to boost their invention level to 103. Then, they can discover timeworn components. Timeworn components are the cheapest and highest-experience material to put into an ancient gizmo. Ancient tool gizmo shells are not recommended due to the high cost, with ancient armour gizmo shells also not recommended due to these shells not being able to use timeworn components; instead, use ancient weapon gizmo shells. Timeworn components can be purchased as crates from the Grand Exchange, but the gizmo components must be acquired separately. Completed gizmos can be created at a cost of each, yielding experience at a rate of coins per XP. On average, using the "repeat" button in gizmo creation, it takes about 9 ticks (5.4 seconds) to create a gizmo from scratch and then disassemble it. Thus, about 667 gizmos can be created per hour. This rate does not include the time required to obtain the materials needed to craft ancient gizmo shells. When creating timeworn ancient armour gizmos, experience can be earned in an hour.

The total amount of experience between 86 and 120 is . Using this method and assuming no boosts, one can level between 86 and 120 with , which takes hours. 1,885 ancient gizmos must be created. For example, creating ancient weapon gizmo shells requires the following materials: 37,700 blade parts, 3,770 strong components, 37,700 historic components, and 3,770 classic components.

Creating gizmos benefits from boosts such as torstol incense sticks, which reduce the number of ancient armour gizmos required.

Players who have not unlocked timeworn components should train using combat with an XP capacitor, because experience rates using most lower-levelled materials is not significantly higher than completing ED3 trash runs.

Effigy Incubator is a monthly five-minute Distractions and Diversions event. Constructing unstable effigy (uncharged) gives 2,500 Invention XP each. Each effigy requires 20 enriched nicknacks which also gives about 10 Invention XP each. Usually 160 materials can be gathered to make 8 effigies giving about 22,000 Invention XP a month.

Besides the five-minute monthly event, regular (non-enriched) nicknacks may be obtained at about 30 per minute. Any extra enriched materials or regular (non-enriched) materials can be given to Vicendithas for 1 point each in The Effigy Incubator Reward Shop.
